hero.title: AI Collaboration Workspace
hero.coreValue: AI executes. Humans set the boundary.
hero.supportingText:
Different tasks require different AI collaboration methods.
Choose Conversation, Skill, or Human Gate by uncertainty, repetition, subjectivity, and decision risk.

humanGate.label: HUMAN GATE
humanGate.text: When evidence cannot support a unique decision.

collaborationModes.title: Collaboration Modes Overview
collaborationModes.introduction: Different task natures require different AI collaboration methods.

creative.taskNature: Subjective output · No single correct answer
creative.name: Reference-to-Style

expandedSections.title: Conversational Prototyping
expandedSections.introduction: When requirements are still unstable, use conversation and interactive prototypes to progressively narrow the problem instead of prematurely freezing unvalidated judgments into a Skill.

problem.label: Problem
problem.text: Direction, constraints, and success criteria are not yet stable.

items.text: Set direction · Make trade-offs · Judge assumptions

prematureFreeze.label: Premature Freeze Path
prematureFreeze.insight: The problem is not always unstable AI execution; it can be AI consistently executing a rule that was never validated.

items.name: Problem Boundary
items.text: What actually needs to be solved

items.name: Product Constraints
items.text: What must remain and what can be removed

convergence.label: Convergence Decision
convergence.text: Exploration does not end when there is ‘an answer’; it ends when the key judgments are stable enough.

paths.condition:
Multi-stage · Independently reviewable

expandedSections.title: PRD Collaboration Agent
expandedSections.introduction: Orchestrate PRD generation and independent review into a collaboration flow controlled by a Human Gate. Prototype-to-PRD is the starting point in this capability’s evolution.

problem.label: Problem
problem.text: A prototype can express observable behavior, but it cannot prove complete product rules. After PRD generation, issues may remain in states, permissions, exceptions, and prototype consistency; AI must not fill in unconfirmed product semantics on its own.

stages.name: Prototype-to-PRD Skill
stages.description: Extract observable facts from a prototype, identify specification gaps, and transform confirmed content into a PRD.

stages.name: PRD Review Skill
stages.description: Independently inspect product logic, states, permissions, exceptions, and prototype ↔ PRD consistency.

stages.name: PRD Collaboration Agent
stages.description: A lightweight orchestration layer that connects the generation and review Skills and manages pauses, resumption, and targeted re-review.

method.label: Agent Flow
method.introduction: This is a lightweight Skill-orchestration Agent. It does not autonomously plan complex tasks; it calls two validated Skills, pauses at a Human Gate, and resumes after a human decision.
method.note: A Human Gate can trigger early at any stage; the Agent does not mechanically preserve a fixed sequence.

evidence.alt: Publication-safe synthetic document comparison prototype with sources, working copy, and completion control
evidence.label: Prototype Input

groups.label: Not Uniquely Determined
groups.heading: Not determined by the prototype alone

architecture.label: Inside the PRD Generation Skill
architecture.introduction: This layer is responsible for generating specifications from the prototype. After generation, the work moves into independent review and Agent orchestration.

layers.name: Core Skill
layers.responsibility: Evidence reading, gap detection, and uniqueness testing

layers.name: Company Rules
layers.responsibility: PRD structure, specification granularity, annotations, and documentation standards

layers.name: Platform Rules
layers.responsibility: Confirmed platform states, permissions, and behavioral invariants
layers.condition: Only when object and scope apply

routing.determined: Existing evidence or an applicable rule determines a unique answer

boundary.label: Not Uniquely Determined → Human Gate
boundary.text: Business semantics that evidence cannot uniquely determine stay out of Skill defaults; people decide them and keep them within the specific project.

humanGateEvidence.label: Human Gate Evidence
humanGateEvidence.finding: A missing piece of information was found: the current materials did not define whether a particular role participates in the feature.
humanGateEvidence.question: Instead of adding a permission rule directly, the Agent first asked whether this role belonged to the current requirement scope.

decision.label: Human Decision
decision.text: The role was outside the current requirement scope, so it was classified as Out of Scope and no new permission rule was added.

principle.label: Product Principle
principle.text: Missing information ≠ something that must be filled in. First determine whether it belongs to the current scope.

humanGateEvidence.example: Synthetic reconstruction: while generating the PRD, existing evidence could not uniquely determine whether a separate reviewer role belonged to the current AI enrichment scope.

validation.label: Validation
validation.text: The Human Gate interrupted the complete E2E flow. Execution resumed after the Human Decision, and targeted re-review closed all four findings. The public case is a synthetic reconstruction based on observed product workflow patterns, not a production metric.

result.label: Result
result.text: The goal of this Agent is not to make AI complete more work autonomously, but to let two reusable Skills collaborate continuously within explicit boundaries and hand control back to people when product judgment is required.

expandedSections.title: Reference-to-Style
expandedSections.introduction: Turn failures in open-ended visual generation into inspectable, reusable generation rules.

problem.label: What failed
problem.text: Open-ended style generation tends to preserve too much non-essential information.

goal.label: Why this goal
goal.text: The goal is not to reproduce the photo as faithfully as possible. It is to rebuild a fixed loose-line style with the fewest visual cues that still preserve subject identity and the key interaction.

items.title: Content admission failed
items.text: Non-essential information entered the final image.

items.title: Feature compression was insufficient
items.text: The result retained too much subject structure.

items.title: Visual primitives were under-constrained
items.text: Eyes, fur, and complete contours were still reconstructed; visual primitives needed to limit the available cues.

evidence.alt: Original photo of a long-haired Chihuahua used as the Reference-to-Style input
evidence.label: Source Photo
evidence.title: Original input photo
evidence.description: Provides subject identity, proportion, and relationship cues.

evidence.alt: Simplified result still containing excessive body contours and local features
evidence.label: Early Output
evidence.title: Photo detail was over-reconstructed
evidence.description: The model still completed eyes, fur, contours, and other full visual information. It looked more realistic, but did not match the target Style Profile.

evidence.label: Product Rule
evidence.title: Feature Compression + Visual Primitive
evidence.description: Do not repeatedly subtract from a complete photo; reconstruct from the essential identity and relationship cues.

evidence.alt: Intermediate generated result with reduced scene content and local detail
evidence.label: Constrained Result
evidence.title: Limited cues preserve the key relationship
evidence.description: Reduce non-essential detail while retaining subject recognition and interaction cues.

items.alt: Second source photo of a white Chihuahua sitting behind a table
items.label: Source Photo

items.alt: Second early output still reconstructing the eyes, contours, and body structure in full
items.label: Early Output

items.alt: Second constrained output retaining recognizable Chihuahua cues with fewer lines
items.label: Constrained Result

result.label: Result
result.text: Rules constrain the generation boundary, but Human Evaluation decides final acceptance.

sharedPrinciple.title: A Shared Judgment Pattern
sharedPrinciple.introduction: The Human Gate appears at different points in each task. In both cases, people take over only when the available evidence cannot determine a unique answer.

aiSpace.heading: Structured Task · PRD Collaboration Agent
aiSpace.description: The Agent orchestrates generation and independent review. When review finds an issue that existing evidence cannot uniquely determine, the Human Gate decides before revision and targeted re-review continue.

humanSpace.heading: Creative Task · Reference-to-Style
humanSpace.description: AI turns failure into Feature Compression and Visual Primitive rules. Human Evaluation decides whether the result preserves the right identity and relationship.

humanGate.label: SHARED JUDGMENT BOUNDARY
humanGate.text: When evidence or rules cannot support a unique answer, AI stops inferring and a person takes over the decision.

sharedPrinciple.closingPrinciple: The collaboration boundary is not defined by whether AI can generate an answer, but by whether the available evidence can justify a unique judgment.

footer.closingStatement: Design the right boundary between AI capability and human judgment.
